Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 LAAS.No.11 of 2015
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) Heard learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer and Sri V.Satyam Reddy, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants.

2. This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short 'the Act') is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer aggrieved by the order and decree dated 03.11.2010 passed in LAOP.No.480 of 2009 on the file of the IX Additional District Judge, Kamareddy (hereinafter referred to as "the Reference Court').
3. In nut-shell, the facts of the case are that lands to an extent of Acs.4.09 guntas in Sy.Nos.925 and 415 of Posanipet Village, Sadashivnagar Mandal, Nizamabad District, belonging to the respondents/claimants were acquired for the purpose of providing house sites to weaker sections of society; that Draft Notification under Section 4(1) of the Act and Draft Declaration under Section 2 AKS, J & LNA, J 6 of the Act were published in A.P. Gazette on 20.07.1999, invoking the urgency clause under Section 17(1) of the Act; and that after following the procedure prescribed under the Act and after conducting enquiry, the Land Acquisition Officer passed an Award, fixing the market value of the acquired lands @ Rs.20,000/- per acre.

4. Not being satisfied with the compensation granted in the Award, the respondents/claimants sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the same was referred to the competent civil Court and numbered as L.A.O.P.No.480 of 2009 on the file of the Reference Court.
5. Before the Reference Court, on behalf of the respondents/claimants, P.Ws.1 to 3 were examined and Exs.A-1 to A-4 were marked.
On behalf of the appellant-Referring Officer, R.W-1 was examined and Ex.B-1-Award was marked.

6. On due appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence available on record, the Reference Court enhanced the market value of the acquired from Rs.20,000/- per acre to Rs.60,000/- per 3 AKS, J & LNA, J square yard, apart from granting all the statutory benefits under the Act to the The Land Acquisition Officer vs Sutari Narayana And13 Ots on 30 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65828298/
1 respondents/claimants.

sentences.text: Aggrieved thereby, the present appeal is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer.

7. Learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer contended that the Reference Court failed to note that the claimants have not established their claim for enhancement of compensation; that the Reference Court has not properly appreciated the documentary evidence adduced before it; that the Land Acquisition Officer has rightly fixed the market value of the subject acquired lands taking into consideration all the statistics pertaining to relevant period of three years prior to 4(1) notification; that the Reference Court erred in enhancing the market value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer; and that therefore, the impugned order is irregular and contrary to law and accordingly, the same is liable to be set aside.

8. Learned counsel for the respondents-claimants contended that the Reference Court has appreciated the evidence adduced by the respondents/claimants in support of their claim for 4 AKS,
J & LNA, J enhancement of compensation in a correct perspective and on finding that the respondents/claimants were able to establish their claim for enhancement of market value of the subject acquired lands by adducing cogent evidence to that effect, rightly enhanced the market value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer and passed the impugned order fixing market value of the acquired lands on acreage basis.

Therefore, the impugned order passed by the Reference Court is based on proper appreciation of facts of the case and the evidence adduced before it and as such, the same needs no interference by this Court.
9.
The respondents/claimants to substantiate their claim for enhancement of market value of the acquired lands have adduced evidence by way of examining PWs-1 to 3 and got marked Exs.A-1 to A-4.

10. Admittedly, Exs.A-1 and A-2-sale deeds are pertaining to sale of lands in Ramareddy Village,
whereunder an extent of 128 square yards and 247 square yards were sold for Rs.2,600/- and Rs.5,000/-, respectively.
In other words, the lands sold under 5 AKS, J & LNA, J Exs.A-1 and A-2 works out to Rs.98,312/- per acre and Rs.97,975/- per acre, respectively.
The respondents/claimants have sought to rely upon Exs.A-1 and A-2-sale deeds in support of their claim for enhancement of market value of the subject acquired lands.
11. The subject lands under acquisition are situated at Posanipet Village, Nizamabad District.

It is the case of the claimants that the subject acquired lands in Posanipet Village are near to Ramareddy and Kamareddy Villages i.e., the subject acquired lands are adjacent to the roads leading to Ramareddy and Kamareddy Villages.

The claimants have not stated the exact or at least approximate distance between the subject acquired lands in Posanipet Village and the lands covered under Exs.A-1 and A-2, which are situated at Ramareddy Village.

12. It is known from Nizamabad District map that the distance between Posanipet Village and Kamareddy Village is about 10 kms and the distance between Posanipet Village and Ramareddy Village is about 4 kms.
In such a case, the sale deeds under Exs.A-1 and 6 AKS, J & LNA, J A-2 cannot be adopted for fixing the market value of the subject acquired lands.

sentences.text: As regards the other exhibits marked on behalf of the respondents/claimants before the Reference Court, i.e., Exs.A-3 and A-4, they go to show that Ex.A-3 is the judgment and decree in O.P.No.5 of 2005, whereunder the Senior Civil Judge, Kamareddy, for the land acquired thereunder in Posanipet Village in the year 1994, has awarded Rs.8/- per square yard, which works out to Rs.38,720/- per acre.

14. Ex.A-4 is the judgment and decree in O.P.No.6 of 2005, whereunder the Senior Civil Judge,
Kamareddy, for the land acquired thereunder in Padmajiwadi Village in the year 1994, has awarded Rs.8/- per square yard, which works out to Rs.38,720/- per acre.
It is not the case of the claimants that the subject acquired lands are in the vicinity of Padmajiwadi Village, therefore, Ex.A-4 is of no help to the claimants.

15. Now, coming to Ex.B-1-Award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer, it shows that the Land Acquisition Officer has 7 AKS, J & LNA, J fixed the market value of the subject acquired lands adopting a sale deed pertaining to Sy.No.140/6 of Posanipet Village, by observing that the nature,
fertility, utility, etc., of the subject acquired lands and the land sold under the said sale deed are similar.
On behalf of the Land Acquisition Officer, Senior Assistant of Revenue Division Officer was examined as R.W-1.
He failed to produce and get the adopted sale deed referred in Ex.B-1-Award marked as an exhibit before the Reference Court.

When it is the specific case of the claimant that the land covered under adopted sale deed by the Land Acquisition Officer is far away from the subject acquired lands and the potentiality of the subject acquired lands, being situated in middle of the village, is higher than the land covered under the adopted sale deed, it was for the Land Acquisition Officer to record the statements of the vendor and vendee of the adopted sale deed in order to prove the bona fides of the said adopted sale deed and also to show that the nature, fertility, etc., of the land covered under the said sale deed are similar to the subject acquired lands.
But, the Land Acquisition Officer did not choose to take such steps.
R.W-1 deposed reiterating the contents of Ex.B-1- 8 AKS, J & LNA, J Award.
It is pertinent to note here that in Ex.B-1-Award, the Land Acquisition Officer has observed that the subject acquired lands are highly potential and are feasible for construction of houses.
Since it is not R.W-1 who has physically inspected the subject acquired lands, conducted award enquiry, etc., his evidence is of no help to prove the case of the Land Acquisition Officer.

Further, the very purpose of acquisition of the subject lands, i.e., for providing house sites to weaker sections of society, strengthens the case of the claimants regarding the potentiality of the subject acquired lands for house sites the same being surrounded by schools,
banks, etc.
16.
This Court in order to assess and fix the market value of the subject acquired lands has thoroughly perused Ex.A-3.

The subject lands covered under Ex.A-3 are located in Posanipet Village,
which were acquired in the year 1994.

In the said judgment- Ex.A-3, the Reference Court, on due appreciation of the evidence placed on record, has fixed the market value of the lands therein @
Rs.8/-per square yard, which amounts to Rs.38,720/- per acre.
No appeal is preferred before this Court against the said judgment either by the Land Acquisition Officer or by the claimants therein.
9 AKS, J & LNA, J
Therefore, the judgment under Ex.A-3 is said to have attained finality.

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, the market value of the subject acquired lands can be fixed basing on Ex.A-3.

It is to be noted that the lands covered under Ex.A-3 were acquired in the year 1994,
whereas the subject acquired lands are acquired in the year 1999 by invoking the urgency clause under Section 17(1) of the Act.
Thus, there is a time gap of five years between the aforesaid two acquisitions.

The market value of the subject acquired lands would have definitely increased when compared to their value in the year 1994 and as such, escalation has to be added to the value reflected in Ex.A-3 while fixing the market value of the subject acquired lands.

18. As regards the quantum of escalation to be added, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a catena of decisions held that the escalation has to be given based on the location of the lands, i.e., whether it is urban, semi-urban or rural.

Admittedly, the subject acquired lands are in semi-urban area,
therefore, the appropriate 10 AKS, J & LNA, J cumulative escalation would be 7.5% per annum on Rs.38,720/-, which for five years works out to Rs.52,101/- per acre.
19. In the light of the above facts and circumstances of the case, this Court holds that the escalation added by the Reference Court is on a higher side and the same needs to be modified.
20. Accordingly, this Appeal is allowed in part, modifying the impugned order of the Reference Court and fixing the market value of the subject acquired lands @ Rs.52,101/- per acre.
It is needless to say that the respondents/claimants are entitled to all the statutory benefits under the Act on the market value of the subject acquired lands fixed @ Rs.52,101/- per acre.
21. As a sequel, Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
